newsitem.title: Singapore: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Buyers emerge as diesel offer dip.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Buyers emerge as diesel offer dip.

text.p: Gas oil buyers reemerged in Singapore on Tuesday as sellers lowered their offers from Monday when they were asking for more than $22 a barrel, traders said.
They said the market was consolidating at the $21.50-$22.00 range, but some said that the next support level could be around $21.20, free-on-board (fob) basis.
Traders noted that there is sporadic demand from China and Indonesia, while the closed arbitrage from the Mediterranean was helping to put regional supplies under control.
They said most Mediterranean cargoes were being absorbed by traders shortcovering into India who had bought 19 cargoes in its tender for July delivery.

Traders said buyers were now looking to buy from the MidEast with a cargo heard sold this week by a national oil company to a US trader for mid-July lifting at a 35-cent-per-barrel premium to MidEast spot quotes, fob.

On Tuesday, two cargoes were traded--one for July 13-17 between a Malaysian trader and a Swiss trader at $21.50 and the second at $21.90 between a Malaysian trader and a Singapore trader for July 18-22 lifting.
The Malaysian trader continued to offer at $21.50 for mid-July lifting at $21.50, facing two Singapore traders.
A major was heard bidding at $21.20 for July 9-13, seen as the next bottom level.
Jet fuel was also actively discussed but was not traded. A European major was offering at $24.60 for July 17-21, facing bids at $23.00, $23.60-$23.70.

Nepal's kerosene tender for July 21-31 delivery saw a low offer of less than $195 per tonne, cost-and-freight basis, from a European major. This was lower than its last purchase at $199.37 for July 1-10 delivery from Vitol.
